# Morse — The signal studio: full product notes

Morse Studio is a static client-side web application. The website provides an overview, text-to-Morse encoder, Morse-to-text decoder, alphabet/prosign reference, practice quiz and Cipher Lab.

## Morse translation
International Morse letters A-Z, digits 0-9, punctuation and common prosigns are supported. A slash separates words. An app-specific Arabic/Urdu extension table is included; it is a convenience mapping and must not be treated as a single globally standardized encoding. Audio timing exposes WPM and Farnsworth spacing and tone frequency. Light and vibration output are best-effort device capabilities. Tap-key controls accept dots, dashes, letter gaps and word gaps.

## Cipher Lab: Codebook
A personal codebook maps words to emoji sequences. Templates can be customized, unknown words use a character-level fallback alphabet, and JSON import/export is available. This mode is reversible obfuscation and does not provide confidentiality against someone who can inspect the mapping or infer it.

## Cipher Lab: Secure
The application uses Web Crypto AES-256-GCM. A key is derived from the user's passphrase using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations. Each encryption generates a cryptographically random 16-byte salt and 12-byte GCM nonce. The JSON envelope is represented as emoji pairs (hexadecimal nibbles encoded with emoji). Decryption authenticates the message; a wrong passphrase or modified ciphertext fails authentication. The passphrase is not stored. Do not reuse weak passwords. Secure URL fragments are bearer secrets and should be shared privately.

## Data handling
No server receives plaintext, passphrases, codebooks or ciphertext during normal operation. The app may persist theme, encrypted saved codebook and a short local history in browser storage. A panic wipe clears the app's local storage and caches on the current browser origin.

## Accessibility and offline
Semantic controls, visible focus styles, labels and reduced-motion CSS are included. A service worker caches the application shell for offline use after first visit. Browser/device support varies for vibration, audio and screen flashing.
